title: Uptake of Progressive Wage Mark Accreditation and Its Impact on Volume of Business
what_it_is: Uptake of Progressive Wage Mark Accreditation and Its Impact on Volume of Business

sections.label: Progressive Wage Mark accreditation and procurement
sections.summary: Over 3,600 firms are PW Mark-accredited, MOM encourages procurement from them, and Government tenders require the mark since 1 March 2023, extending to quotations from 1 March 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Since the Progressive Wage Mark's (PW Mark's) launch in January 2023, more than 3,600 firms have been accredited with the PW Mark.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) encourages service buyers to procure from PW Mark-accredited suppliers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: However, MOM does not track the number of service buyers that have chosen to do business exclusively with companies accredited with the PW Mark.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, based on our recent business sentiment survey, nine in 10 businesses polled indicated that they will prioritise purchases from corporate suppliers with the PW Mark, in support of our lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: As a major service buyer, the Government has taken the lead in making the PW Mark a contractual obligation for tenders since 1 March 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: This requirement will be extended to include Government quotations from 1 March 2024.

sections.label: Workers covered by PW Mark firms
sections.summary: More than 3,600 accredited firms hire about 56,000 low-wage workers, against a low-wage worker segment sized at about 283,000 in the 2021 Tripartite Workgroup Report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To the Member's first supplementary question on how many workers are covered, I mentioned earlier that we have got more than 3,600 firms that are accredited with the PW Mark and that collectively, they hire approximately 56,000 low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If you think about the percentages, in the 2021 Tripartite Workgroup Report, we sized the low-wage worker segment to be about 283,000 workers.

sections.label: Government and contract re-negotiations
sections.summary: Contract re-negotiations are commercial negotiations, so the Government does not intervene in contracting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To the Member's question on contract re-negotiations, these are commercial negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Therefore, the Government does not intervene in contracting.
